estimator_variances.csia_may_use_reason: deliberately excluded from diagnosis. CSIA must not consume the estimator it is meant to be independent of. Logged for the autopilot-vs-CSIA comparison required by S9, and for nothing else.

reasons: the entire gps_fault evidence set is ['phys_gps'] (csia/diagnosis/bayes.py CAUSES), so attribution has exactly one supporting feature
P['gps'] gate is 'gvalid * (1.0 if tau > 3.0 else 0.0)', so the one supporting feature is multiplied by the flag the fault zeroes
no GNSS channel is usable on ANY tick of the fix-loss window on either platform, so the phys_gps residual (_gps_fd_vel - vel) has neither input
the relations that DO survive use no GNSS input, so nothing makes them sensitive to a GNSS fault: they would be non-discriminating

the one fault-sensitive quantity that survives, estimator.variances, is contractually forbidden (csia_may_use: false -- deliberately excluded from diagnosis. CSIA must not consume the estimator it is meant to be independent of. Logged for t...), and was observed usable on {'ardupilot': 0.0, 'px4': 0.0} of fix-loss ticks anyway

4B_gate_event_likelihood.Z: the missingness reason on gnss.position (NO_3D_FIX vs present) -- a categorical event, not a residual
4B_gate_event_likelihood.reason: one fault flight per platform cannot calibrate P(Z|H,C), and no calibration/test split is possible; the brief's permitted fallback is taken

4C_sequential_detector.note: validated on Phase-2 offline streams; applying it to current-stack traces needs mu0/sigma0 re-derived on CLEAN current-stack data, for which 28 flights exist, so calibration/test separation IS possible here

parameters.decision_h_rule: smallest h from a fixed grid for which the CLEAN NOMINAL ARM produces zero alarms. Evaluated on the clean arm only, never on a fault outcome — the same constraint rule B2's k is chosen by.
parameters.detector: one-sided CUSUM on the standardised PRE-TRANSFORM residual (OnlineTrustLayer._lam, read-only)

evidence.controlled_by: presence/absence of SET_MESSAGE_INTERVAL on the consumer's own link, both arms in the same boot

4E_operating_regime.reason: crossing the 2.0 m/s heading_course gate needs a new commanded-trajectory path in the rig and a new campaign. Feasible on ArduPilot, not cheap, and the brief forbids letting it delay the main experiment

decision_basis: the brief allows a reduced experiment only if structural rescue, the sequential detector AND transport-starvation control are all feasible. Structural rescue fails, so no reduced form is available either.
what_this_is: MAER feasibility audit -- run before any MAER implementation exists, and allowed to return no
